headline: Fed day with WTI back through $100 and the euro at a 52-week low: the duration rally that fueled the beta bounce is being taxed by oil and the dollar before Powell even speaks.
summary: The tape handed off from New York to Asia and got more violent, not less. KOSPI +6.6% in a single session after a -12.7% month (z=-1.84), Taiwan +2.0%, Nikkei +1.1% — the global semi washout is being bought hard, following SOXX +3.9%, AMD +5.5%, TSM +2.9% and MU +2.8% in the prior US session. But the won didn't confirm: USD/KRW +1.1% to 1339.8 on the same day Korea ripped. That is a domestic squeeze, not foreign money arriving. The same split runs through everything today — equity beta recovering off washout lows (SMH/SPY z=-1.45 turning up, SPHB/SPLV turning up from z=-2.0) while the macro plumbing tightens underneath it. DXY 102.40, 97th percentile of the year. EURUSD 1.1128, the 0th percentile, a fresh 52-week low and -2.2% on the month. USD/MXN z=1.87 at the 97th percentile, +5.1% on the month.

What changed overnight versus yesterday's read is oil. Yesterday's -5.5% Brent flush, which looked like a gift to the inflation print, lasted one session: WTI +1.8% to 101.74, back above the century mark, +9.9% on the month and +77.2% YTD; natural gas +14.1% in a day; oil/gold +2.2% to the 95th percentile and +89.5% YTD. That reloads the one thing the Fed cannot ignore at 2pm. The inflation composite is -47. Five-year breakevens are 2.45%, +11bp on the month and turning up. Headline CPI is running +106bp YTD with a month-move z of 0.65 and rising acceleration (+0.61), even as core decelerates. The 30-year mortgage is 7.32%, 94th percentile. Against that, the entire month-long duration rally — 10y 4.99% (-18bp, acc z=-1.94), 5y 4.82% (-16bp, acc -2.03), 10y real 2.64% (-19bp, acc -2.02) — is the single pillar holding up the high-beta bounce, and the front end is refusing to play: 2y 4.70%, +2bp yesterday, +123bp YTD; 3m bill 4.22% at the 91st percentile; 2s10s 29bp, 17th percentile, flattening 7bp on the month. Rates composite -40.

The good news is that nothing in the risk plumbing is broken. VIX 17.49 at the 23rd percentile of its year, MOVE 97.87 and back under 100 (-4.2% on the week), HYG +0.5% with HYG/IEF +0.5%, BKLN at the 93rd percentile, credit & vol composite +4. Equal-weight is doing work the index isn't: RSP +3.0% on the month with RSP/SPY at a z=1.71 move and the highest acceleration on the board (+3.01), though the ratio itself has rolled over — the one caveat. The growth pulse is quietly firming: UPS +12.9% on the month (z=1.69, acc 2.06), FDX +7.4%, DJT +5.0% and turning up, IYT/SPY acceleration +2.54, copper +1.1% on the month with copper/gold at the 100th percentile of its year. Risk regime -15, unchanged from yesterday's improvement.

The damage is concentrated and it is accelerating in the wrong direction in two places. Precious metals: gold -0.4% to 4,058.9, 7th percentile and 10.3% below its 200-day; silver -12.2% on the month (z=-1.42, 24.6% below its 200-day); platinum -10.6%; gold/silver +10.9% on the month with acceleration still positive at 1.07. That unwind is not finished, and it is happening while oil rips — this is a positioning liquidation, not a deflation signal. And EM ex-Asia is where the dollar bites: EEM/SPY z=-1.91 at the 16th percentile, TUR -15.3% on the month, EWZ -20.1% on the week, KWEB -5.9% and at the 0th percentile, Hang Seng -6.3%. Single-name dispersion remains brutal — BA -10.7% in a session to the 0th percentile, META -17.5% on the month with acceleration z=-3.03, NFLX and UBER both at the 0th percentile, REMX -18.7% — while LMT sits +19.9% on the month at a z=2.59 move with acceleration 2.73 inside an ITA at the 15th percentile. Crowding on both tails.

good.text: Vol and credit are not validating the tightening: VIX 17.49 at the 23rd percentile, MOVE back under 100 at 97.87 (-3.8% on the week), HYG +0.5% with HYG/IEF +0.5%, BKLN at the 93rd percentile of its year. Credit & vol composite +4 — no stress signal into a Fed decision.

The global semi washout is being bought: KOSPI +6.6% in a day off a z=-1.84 month, Taiwan TAIEX +2.0%, Nikkei +1.1%, after TSM +2.9%, AMD +5.5%, MU +2.8% and SOXX +3.9% in the prior US session. SMH/SPY turning up from z=-1.45.

The month-long rates deceleration is still intact and is what is financing the beta bounce: 10y 4.99% (-18bp 1m, acc z=-1.94), 5y 4.82% (-16bp, acc -2.03), 30y 5.30% (-19bp), 10y real 2.64% (-19bp, acc -2.02).

Growth pulse is firming under the surface: UPS +12.9% on the month (z=1.69, acc 2.06), FDX +7.4%, Dow Transports +5.0% and turning up, IYT/SPY acceleration +2.54, copper/gold at the 100th percentile of its 52 weeks.

Breadth is improving even if the ratio stalled: S&P equal-weight +3.0% on the month, RSP/SPY at a z=1.71 move with the board's highest acceleration (+3.01), IWM +1.6% on the week and Russell 2000 turning up.
The yuan is quietly the strongest major: USD/CNY -0.9% on the month to the 0th percentile, with AUD +0.4% on the week and copper +1.4% — Asia's cyclical complex isn't confirming the dollar squeeze.

bad.text: Crude retook $100 the day after the flush: WTI +1.8% to 101.74 (+9.9% 1m, +77.2% YTD), natural gas +14.1% in a session, oil/gold at the 95th percentile and +89.5% YTD. The de-escalation relief lasted one session and the inflation composite sits at -47.

The front end won't cooperate into the decision: 2y 4.70% (+2bp, +123bp YTD, 86th percentile), 3m bill 4.22% at the 91st percentile, 2s10s 29bp at the 17th percentile and flattening 7bp on the month, 30y mortgage 7.32% at the 94th percentile. Rates composite -40.
Dollar as wrecking ball: DXY 102.40 at the 97th percentile, EURUSD 1.1128 at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks (-2.2% 1m), USD/MXN z=1.87 at the 97th percentile, USD/KRW +1.1% even on a +6.6% KOSPI day.

The precious metals unwind is still accelerating: gold 10.3% below its 200-day at the 7th percentile, silver -12.2% on the month (z=-1.42), platinum -10.6%, gold/silver +10.9% with acceleration +1.07, GDXJ -14.6% on the month.
EM ex-Asia and China keep leaking: EEM/SPY z=-1.91 at the 16th percentile, KWEB -5.9% on the month at the 0th percentile, Hang Seng -6.3%, Turkey -15.3%, EWZ -20.1% on the week.

Dispersion is at wreckage levels: BA -10.7% in a day to the 0th percentile, META -17.5% on the month with acceleration z=-3.03 inside an XLC at the 0th percentile, NFLX and UBER both at the 0th percentile, REMX -18.7%.

trades.name: Oil services (OIH) as the un-extended way to own $100 crude
trades.line: Long OIH: $100 WTI, and OIH is only 3% over its 200d
trades.expr: Buy OIH outright, or Jan OIH 420/470 call spread. Size half the usual energy clip given the sector's run.
trades.thesis: Energy is the only sector with rising relative strength (+10.2% 1m vs S&P), but XLE is 18.0% above its 200-day at the 95th percentile and XOP is 18.7% extended. OIH is up only 3.9% on the month and sits 3.2% over its 200-day with trend turning up — the catch-up leg, not the crowded one.
trades.trigger: WTI +1.8% today to 101.74, back above 100 and +9.9% on the month; OIH +6.2% on the week while XOP was -2.4% yesterday. Oil/gold +2.2% to the 95th percentile.
trades.stop: WTI closes below 95 (gives back the whole month) or OIH breaks its 200-day, now ~3% lower.
trades.target: OIH 455-470 (+12-15%), closing the extension gap versus XOP.

trades.name: Short TLT into the Fed — the duration rally is done
trades.line: Short TLT: oil back >$100, breakevens +11bp, 2y stuck at 4.70%
trades.expr: Short TLT at 81.6, or buy Dec TLT 80/76 put spread. Alternative: pay 10y swaps.
trades.thesis: The 18bp month-long drop in the 10y (acc z=-1.94) and 19bp in the 10y real yield was built on a crude flush and a soft core print. Crude just reversed, 5y breakevens are 2.45% and turning up, headline CPI is accelerating (+106bp YTD, acc z=0.61). A Fed that stays patient on inflation at these oil prices steepens the term premium; a hawkish one bear-flattens. TLT loses either way, and its trend state is still 'down' with 1m acceleration at +1.35 — the bounce is countertrend.
trades.trigger: WTI +1.8% through 100 and natgas +14.1% on the day the FOMC decides; 2y at 4.70% (+123bp YTD) has refused to follow the long end down.
trades.stop: TLT above 84.50 (10y below ~4.80%) or 5y breakevens back under 2.30%.

trades.name: Short EURUSD — 0th percentile with no stabilizer
trades.line: Short EUR 1.1128: 52-wk low, DXY 97th pct, no bid in Europe
trades.expr: Short EURUSD spot at 1.1128; or 3-month 1.09 EUR puts. Stop above 1.1250.
trades.thesis: The euro is at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range, -2.2% on the month (z=-1.05), with DXY at the 97th percentile and USD/CHF at the 92nd. European equities are not offsetting: CAC -2.5% on the month at the 20th percentile, Euro Stoxx -2.4%, EFA/SPY at the 11th percentile. Rate differentials still widen as the US 2y sits at 4.70%.
trades.trigger: EURUSD -0.4% today to a fresh 52-week low on Fed day; DXY +1.2% on the month and holding the 97th percentile.
trades.stop: 1.1250 spot (a dovish Fed that breaks the dollar's 200-day extension of +2.8%).

trades.name: Long Taiwan (EWT) vs short Korea (EWY)
trades.line: Long EWT / short EWY: KOSPI's 6.6% rip isn't confirmed by the won
trades.expr: Long EWT, short EWY, dollar-neutral. Put it on into the Korean strength.
trades.thesis: Both are semi beta, so the pair isolates the quality of the move. Taiwan is in an uptrend 15.6% above its 200-day at the 82nd percentile with relative strength rising (+9.6% 3m); Korea is 'rolling over', -15.9% on the month (z=-1.93) and 2.7% below its 200-day. A 6.6% KOSPI session that comes with a 1.1% weaker won is a local squeeze, not foreign allocation.
trades.trigger: KOSPI +6.6% today while USD/KRW rose 1.1% to 1339.8; TWII +2.0% with TSM +2.9% and the 200-day extension gap at 15.6% vs -2.7%.
trades.stop: EWY/EWT ratio recovers 6% against us, or USD/KRW breaks back below 1300 (genuine inflows).

trades.name: Long silver vs gold — fade a z=1.63 ratio blowout
trades.line: Long SLV / short GLD: gold-silver +10.9% in a month, z=1.63
trades.expr: Long SLV against short GLD, roughly equal notional. Start half size; this is a knife-catch.
trades.thesis: Gold/silver is +10.9% on the month at a z=1.63 move with acceleration still positive (+1.07) and the 78th percentile of its year, while silver sits 24.6% below its 200-day at the 10th percentile with a z=-1.42 month. The macro backdrop — crude +77% YTD, copper at the 91st percentile, copper/gold at a 52-week high — argues the industrial metal shouldn't be liquidating 12% a month against the monetary one.
trades.trigger: Silver -1.0% and gold -0.4% today with the ratio +0.6% to 75.5 — the ratio's acceleration is still rising, so size for a few more days of pain, but the z-scores are at capitulation.
trades.stop: Gold/silver above 82 (another 9%); abandon if GDX_GOLD also rolls back over.
trades.target: Gold/silver back to 66-68 (~12% on the pair).

trades.name: Long XLI vs short XLU — unwind the defensive crowd
trades.line: Long XLI / short XLU: ratio at z=-2.10, XLU acceleration 2.33
trades.expr: Long XLI, short XLU, equal notional. Or express as long SPHB/short SPLV for the same trade with more convexity.
trades.thesis: Industrials/utilities is at a z=-2.10 move with acceleration -1.91 — a two-sigma dislocation. Utilities are +8.5% on the month (z=1.63) with the board's second-highest acceleration (+2.33) yet trade 2.1% BELOW their 200-day and at the 48th percentile: that is yield-chasing, not leadership. Meanwhile the growth pulse is turning — transports +5.0% on the month, UPS +12.9%, FDX +7.4%, IYT/SPY acceleration +2.54 — and the defensive complex (XLP acc 1.89, SPLV 2.35, USMV 1.57) is maximally crowded.
trades.trigger: Defensives gave back ground in the prior session (XLP -0.9%, COST -1.3%, WMT -0.8%) while SPHB/SPLV turned up 3.1% from a z=-2.0 washout; today's Asia beta bid extends it.
trades.stop: XLI/XLU makes a new low (ratio below 3.75) or the 10y breaks above 5.15%, which re-ignites the bond-proxy bid for the wrong reason.

trades.name: Short LMT vs long ITA — fade the single-name defense squeeze
trades.line: Short LMT / long ITA: LMT z=2.59 inside a 15th-pct sector
trades.expr: Short LMT, long ITA at ~1.5x LMT notional. Or buy Dec LMT 600 puts financed by ITA calls.
trades.thesis: LMT is +19.9% on the month at a z=2.59 move with the highest acceleration on the board (+2.73) and 10.8% above its 200-day, sitting inside an aerospace & defense sector that is -3.5% on the month, 9.9% below its 200-day, at the 15th percentile and in a downtrend with relative strength -19.1% over three months. Either the sector catches up or the single name gives it back; the pair pays on convergence and hedges a geopolitical escalation.
trades.trigger: LMT -1.9% in the prior session after a +13.5% week — the first crack in a two-sigma move; ITA -0.5% and still basing at the 15th percentile.
trades.stop: LMT makes a new high above 650 with ITA failing to follow (a genuine order-book event, not positioning).
trades.target: 10-12% on the spread as LMT's z normalizes toward 1.
